subject.title: fix(acp): exit help and EOF cleanly

question: Should ACP intentionally reject pre-Gateway stdin once buffered startup input exceeds 1 MiB, and is that limit guaranteed to stop applying once the Gateway-connected SDK reader owns the stream?
rationale: The branch introduces a new input-size failure mode in a transport bridge while fixing hangs; code review alone cannot choose the compatible ACP behavior or acceptable operational tradeoff.

options.title: Confirm bounded startup buffering
options.body: Accept the 1 MiB pre-Gateway cap after confirming that it is the intended ACP contract and that the monitor is retired once normal SDK consumption begins.

options.title: Prove and narrow the handoff
options.body: Add lifecycle coverage for large post-connect input and adjust monitor ownership or error behavior if the cap can affect normal connected sessions.

options.title: Pause the buffering change
options.body: Land only the lazy-import help fix later and redesign EOF observation if the intended ACP buffering contract is not yet settled.

recommendation.title: Prove and narrow the handoff
recommendation.body: Add lifecycle coverage for large post-connect input and adjust monitor ownership or error behavior if the cap can affect normal connected sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The current PR author is also the assigned participant for this ACP lifecycle change; broader current-main ownership could not be established from the supplied material.
